parts.title: The TORCH Test: Which Glass Lets Only SOME Light Through? (Part 1) | Transparent and Translucent
parts.description:
Clear glass, frosted glass, a wooden door: which one lets only some light pass through? Shine a torch, hide a robot, and be the light! Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: transparency.

In this part:
• The torch test: a torch, a sheet, a white card
• Look closer: the torch on clear glass (a bright spot; the robot seen clearly)
• HOLD ON! Is it a good test if the torch moves?
• Look closer: the torch on frosted glass (a soft glow; a blurry robot)
• Be the light: from the torch, through clear glass and frosted glass
• Spot the hidden goldfish!

Key words: transparent, frosted glass, translucent.
Watch Part 2: it is white, so can light pass through a wooden door? Last episode: a metal ship floats but a metal spoon sinks. Why?

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

Singapore Primary 3 Science (2023 syllabus): Diversity of materials: transparency (Chapter 3, p. 58). See-through, blurry or blocked? Light and materials: transparent, translucent and opaque. Also fits US NGSS 1-PS4-3 (Grade 1 to 3).
Safety: never shine a torch at anyone's eyes, and never look at the Sun. In this video an adult holds the glass and switches on the torch.
Try it at home: find one translucent thing at home and show someone at home.
Singapore and the US: the glass doors on an MRT platform are transparent: you can clearly see the train behind them. The frosted glass of a bathroom window is translucent. In the US (Grade 1 to 3): a torch is a flashlight, a frosted shower door is translucent, and you test materials the same way: change one thing, keep the rest the same.

parts.title: It Is WHITE. So Can Light Pass Through a Wooden Door? (Part 2) | Opaque
parts.description:
A wooden door, painted white. A torch shines on it. How much light passes through? Be the light of a lamp at night and find out! Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: transparency.

In this part:
• Look closer: the torch on a white door (a bright front, nothing behind)
• Opaque: rubber, wood and metal
• Look closer: three sheets, three cards: what transparency means
• Be the light of a lamp: a door, a frosted window, a clear window
• Showdown: find the mistake in Pip's notes (two plastic boxes!)
• A chant to remember it all
• Spot the hidden moth!

Key words: opaque, transparency.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: why isn't a trolley made of glass? Choosing materials.
